acceptance_criteria.criterion: Workflow triggers on push to main and on pull requests
Matrix runs 4 combinations: Node 18/ubuntu, Node 18/windows, Node 22/ubuntu, Node 22/windows
All 4 matrix jobs pass: typecheck, test, build
Build step produces both dist/*.js (ESM) and dist/*.cjs (CJS) output

summary: Workflow triggers on push to main branch and on all pull_request events.
Strategy matrix: node [18, 22] × os [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] = 4 jobs; fail-fast: false so all jobs report independently.

Job steps: checkout → setup-node (with npm cache) → npm ci → npm run typecheck → npm test → npm run build → dist output verification (Node.js cross-platform fs.accessSync check for index.js, index.cjs, changelog/index.js, changelog/index.cjs).
All steps validated locally: typecheck PASS, 229/229 tests PASS, build produces both ESM and CJS output for both entry points.

comments.note: .github/workflows/ci.yml: Consider adding a cache key suffix on the tsup/vitest output (e.g. a hash of package-lock.json) to improve cache hit rate across Node version matrix jobs — currently using default 'cache: npm' which keys on package-lock.json hash alone, which is correct but all 4 matrix jobs will miss cache on first run.

.github/workflows/ci.yml: Coverage results are computed but not uploaded to a coverage service (e.g. Codecov). Low priority for a pre-publish library, but a badge and trend tracking would add value once the package is on npm.

summary: AC1: Triggers confirmed via YAML parse — 'push' (branches: [main]) and 'pull_request' (all PRs).
AC2: Matrix confirmed — node: [18, 22] × os: [ubuntu-latest, windows-latest] = 4 combinations; fail-fast: false.
AC3: Full CI job simulated locally — npm ci (0 vulnerabilities), typecheck (no errors), test (229/229 pass), build (ESM + CJS output for both entry points).
AC4: Dist verify step confirmed — dist/index.js, dist/index.cjs, dist/changelog/index.js, dist/changelog/index.cjs all present and accessible.
YAML structure is valid (7 steps, correct nesting, cross-platform Node fs.accessSync check in verify step).

comments.note: pull_request: trigger has no branch filter — CI runs on PRs targeting any branch, not just main. This is standard best practice and intentional; noting for reviewer awareness.
YAML 'on:' key parses as boolean True in PyYAML (YAML 1.1). This only affects local tooling that consumes the file; GitHub Actions parses it correctly under its own YAML parser. No action needed.

summary: Reviewed .github/workflows/ci.yml. Workflow is well-structured, minimal, and correct. Triggers (push to main + pull_request), 2x2 matrix (Node 18/22 x ubuntu/windows), fail-fast:false, and step ordering all match the ACs and follow GitHub Actions best practices.

Step sequence is correct: checkout → setup-node (npm cache) → npm ci → typecheck → test → build → dist verification. The dist verification uses fs.accessSync with forward-slash paths, which is cross-platform on Windows. pull_request (not pull_request_target) is the correct trigger — no secrets leakage risk. No blocking issues found.

comments.note: No workflow_dispatch trigger is included, meaning the workflow cannot be triggered manually from the GitHub Actions UI. This is a minor convenience omission — useful for re-running CI without a code push, especially during debugging. Low priority.

Actions are pinned to major-version floating tags (@v4) rather than immutable commit SHAs. For a public library publishing to npm, SHA pinning (e.g. actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683) would harden the supply chain. This is a security hardening suggestion, not a blocking issue — major-version tags are standard practice for early-stage libraries.

[documentation-forward] Consider adding a CI status badge to the cli-menu README.md once the workflow is live on GitHub. The badge URL follows the pattern: https://github.com/OWNER/cli-menu/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg
